Day 26 of 100 · Infrastructure Automation

Ansible Variables

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityInfrastructure AutomationPublished journey entry

Variables separate changing data from reusable automation, but precedence decides which value Ansible ultimately uses.

Architecture / mental model

defaults / inventory / play vars / task vars / extra vars → precedence → effective value

How it works

Variables let a playbook keep logic stable while environment-specific values change. Hostnames, ports, package names and environment flags belong in data when they are not part of the reusable task logic.

Ansible has multiple variable sources, so precedence matters. A value can appear correct in one file and still be overridden by a higher-precedence source at runtime.

Extra variables passed with `-e` have very high precedence and are useful for deliberate overrides, but that same power can hide the value the repository appears to declare.

Hands-on reference

ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml -e 'app_port=8080'
ansible-inventory -i inventory.ini --host web01

Verification

Print or debug the effective variable in a lab, then inspect the inventory/host data that supplied it. Do not debug precedence by staring at one YAML file.

Field note / gotcha

A variable defined in the 'obvious' place can still lose to another source. Always reason about the effective value, not the file you last edited.

Security considerations

Do not store secrets in plain variable files. Use Vault or an external secret mechanism and keep secret precedence deliberate.

What I learned

Variables make automation reusable; precedence makes it necessary to know where truth actually comes from.
